comments.author: @asi-system
comments.text:
Let’s be real: this Nissan dealership messed up big time. For a General Manager to throw a total tantrum over ONE honest review and try to attack a small family upholstery shop is pure pettiness. Any legit business gets bad reviews and moves on. The fact that he targeted a creator with over 150k followers makes you wonder if there was an underlying personal motive or if this whole scenario was just a massive miscalculation that blew up in their faces. But as we’ve seen over the last few days, the internet completely backfired on them—the small business now has hundreds of 5-star reviews, and the dealership was forced to apologize after getting crushed by public pressure.

Having been around this industry, this dirty behavior isn't surprising at all. This is literally how traditional dealerships operate: hidden fees, aggressive tactics, warranty tricks, and total disregard for everyday people. And they usually get away with it because local state officials and regulators look the other way as long as the money flows. If this family didn't have a massive social media platform to defend themselves, they would have been quietly crushed by corporate bullying.

This whole mess is a perfect example of how toxic, ego-driven, and broken our current financial and corporate systems are. Small businesses are forced to constantly fight for survival against predatory players.

comments.text: I gave a bad review for a dealership years ago, when I took my Wrangler in for regular service. I had purchased it new from them and the son had taken over the business and was telling the maintenance crew to move faster and get cars in and out faster. I just sat there and watched this happen. I carefully got out of the Jeep and walked back into the service area. I told the receptionist what had happened, she thought I was kidding at first. She realized I was serious and got the manager out to look at it. He then had a mechanic go out and, with my lug nuts, put the wheel back on. She apologized but I was so livid, I sent a message to corporate about the incident and also had the email from the dealership with their apology attached.
